text.1_Genesis, 8_Chapter, 6_Paragraph, 0_Com: "They swarmed throughout the land and multiplied in it"—a highly significant addition to the developmental task of the Noachide world, with which this entire reconstitution of humanity concludes, and whose meaning is revealed by the word רישביל in ביר with the explanation: ברית נחלק לאוירות, a special covenant is given in the various climates and regions. שרץ, as already recognized, is the lowest stage of life, according to the essential characteristic of its appearance, movement, ישרצו המים. By finally adding this attribute to the reproduction and multiplication of the human race, this expression likely presents us with a teeming multitude of the most diverse human manifestations, and thus signifies a diversity and infinite multiplication of the human race in all possible shades as the future development of humanity, and indeed בארץ, on the earth and through the earth and from the earth and under the influence of the manifoldly diverse earth, and not only שרצו בארץ, but also רבו—the entire physical, moral, and spiritual education—also בה under the same influence. What could only be hinted at above in the sentence "While the earth remains, etc." is expressed here. The Noachide humanity received the destiny to spread throughout the entire earth and to become human under the most diverse forms, circumstances, and influences, and to develop the general human character; a diversity and multiplicity that appeared to us in the above context as the new divine plan for the education of the human race (see Raw Hirsch on Genesis 9), which was intended to prevent the necessity of total catastrophes. The diversity is meant to compensate for the deficiencies and thus pave the way for progress towards the goal. The covenant is divided into different atmospheres, therefore the wise men say: "Blessed is He who has given grace to the place in the eyes of its inhabitants," "God has endowed the various regions and types of air with a special covenant" — (perhaps literally: the general covenant of God with humanity is distributed across the most diverse regions) — "Blessed be God, who has bestowed upon each locality a charm in the eyes of its inhabitants!" and they point out how every tribe of people feels comfortable in its homeland, even under the most inhospitable conditions, how the most inhospitable region binds its sons with homesickness when they are abroad and hinders their spiritual development in foreign lands. Man, who believes he rules the earth, is often ruled, even in his innermost being, in spirit, soul, intellect, and language, by the soil that bears and surrounds him, and this diversity is purposeful. Everywhere man can be human, everywhere happy, everywhere the human in man can come to pure fruition. Only one must not apply his standard to another. Therefore, at the end of this reshaping of the earth and humanity, it is said: "Be fruitful and multiply on the earth, through it, in it, with it, etc."
